placement.position_note: SEATED WITH ONE ORIGIN AND ONE BEARING FOR ALL FOURTEEN (T-2050), so no building moves against another. The box is the register's (data/traces/whistler_1808_fort_dearborn.json), read off the commandant's own measured draught at 4.52 px per foot from the 75 ft staff, good to about +/-1.1 ft an edge. THE ORIGIN: the staff's foot, which the register finds at the centre of the parade and within about a foot of the centre of both picket rows, is set on the fort site at local E +1152, N +221 - the Wright 1834 reading of the fort's place that docs/ROADMAP.md S5a cross-checks to 35 m against the modern landmark. That is the SITE, not the second fort's plan: John H. Kinzie (quoted on chicagology_prefire052) says the first fort 'stood upon the same ground as the last Fort' and 'was differently constructed', so the place carries over and nothing of the 1816 geometry does. THE BEARING: the frame's north is set on grid north, which is the register's own inference that the sheet's right is east, from the lake lettered down that margin; the sheet has no north arrow, so the bearing is inferred and adds nothing to it. The second fort's 8 degrees, read off Harrison 1830, is that fort's and is not borrowed. Grid and true north differ here by under half a degree. A CHECK, NOT A FIT: seated so, the outward row's west side stands about 124 ft from the 1812 river (data/terrain/epochs/e1830_natural/river.geojson) and the north-west blockhouse about 65 ft from it; the draught's red-ink '122 feet to River' from the west side and Wilson's '80 feet' from the north-west corner are figures of that size. Carry the datum's +/-20 m on the whole frame.
placement.symbolic_location: First Fort Dearborn, in the frame of Whistler's 1808 draught (register part 'index 6 lines'): E -52.7..+55.3 ft, N -55.5..+55.8 ft of the flagstaff's foot, the main gate in the south side. SEATED (T-2050) with the whole frame: the staff's foot at local E +1152.0, N +221.0, the frame's north on grid north; this record's origin is the box's SW corner.

footprint.note: MEASURED: 108.0 x 111.3 ft, east-west by north-south, between the outer edges of the hatched band the draught draws for each curtain. The band is 8.4-10.2 ft wide, so the two rows stand that far apart.

gate_sides.note: The register reads the main gate's passage running from the inward row out to this one (N -56.6 to -45.6 ft), so the outward row is open there too; no break in this row was read on its own. The wicket gate (index no. 8) Quaife puts 'near the northwestern blockhouse' is not built: the register could not find it on the sheet. The archetype used to centre a gate on its side; since T-3319 gate_offset_m stands it where the draught puts the passage, at E -11.1..-4.9 ft, about 9.3 ft west of this row's centre. WEST WICKET (T-3041): the earlier omission recorded above is superseded. The retrospective Currey birdseye labels western gateway 3 immediately south of northwest blockhouse 4; Quaife locates a wicket near that blockhouse. This supports the west-side occurrence and adjacency, not a precise location on Whistler's draught or a historical width. The south gate and its measured passage remain unchanged.

gate_width_m.note: 6.2 ft, the gap the draught leaves between the two halves of the south range (index no. 7).

gate_offset_m.note: WHERE ALONG THE SOUTH ROW THE MAIN GATE STANDS: -2.83 m (9.3 ft) west of the row's middle. The register (data/traces/whistler_1808_fort_dearborn.json, index no. 7) reads the main gate's passage at E -11.1..-4.9 ft from the staff's foot, the gap between the two halves of the soldiers' barracks; the staff stands at local E +1152 and this row's middle at E +1152.36, so the passage's middle (E -8.0 ft) is this far west of it, and the gate then stands square in the gap the two halves of the south range leave (first_fort_dearborn_soldiers_barracks_sw and _se). Until T-3319 the archetype could only centre a gate, which hung both leaves across the back of the south-east barracks while the passage behind them stood walled; Quaife's 'at the middle of the south side' is the gate's place in the range, which the draught measures. Carries the register's +/-1.1 ft an edge.

gate_overrides.note: WEST WICKET TRIAL (T-3041): a reconstructed 1.50 m cut aligned through both rows in the existing clearance just south of the northwest blockhouse and north of the west officers' range. The offset is chosen from those model neighbors, not measured from the historical drawing. No range, blockhouse, stockade footprint or surveyed placement moves. The single pale-and-rail leaf and posts reuse the generic wicket kit at the existing stockade height; its 1.18 m clear span, details and inward swing are liberties. This does not establish a completion date. Native and picture acceptance remain pending.
